title: The Safehouse of the Green Zone
premise: Noor Yarrow, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of her family aboard Flight 447, is quietly assigned to cases governments want buried. When a passenger jet's records are erased mid-flight and it lands carrying a defector who claims to know who ordered the wipe—and who killed row twelve—Noor becomes both hunter and hunted. Navigating a shadow network of safehouses inside the demilitarized Green Zone, she must extract the defector, Elias Voss, across a border checkpoint before its shift changes, all while suspecting he may be bait designed to flush out survivors of the original conspiracy. In the end, Noor trades her anonymity for justice: she exposes the erased flight's true manifest, loses the man she trusted, and finally gives row twelve a name in the record.
about_author: Ada Nakamura is the pen name of a former aviation-safety analyst who spent a decade reviewing accident reports before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about paper trails, vanished evidence, and the people who refuse to let the dead stay anonymous.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Opening on the anniversary vigil, Noor recalls the family she lost and the case file that officially doesn't exist. Her supervisor hands her a new assignment: an anomaly no agency will claim. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into professional detachment.

chapters.title: The Unattributed
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She reviews the assignment: Flight 9C, whose telemetry began corrupting while still airborne. Every database returns blank. A colleague warns her that unattributed means unwanted. Beat: unease—the erasure feels deliberate, surgical, familiar.

chapters.title: Ghost Altitude
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Reconstructing 9C from radar fragments, she finds the plane landed intact—with one extra passenger logged nowhere: Elias Voss, a signals analyst who defected mid-air. Beat: cold excitement; the first thread that might lead back to row twelve.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Held in a Green Zone safehouse, Voss rehearses his story, knowing half of it is leverage and half is bait. He watches his handlers and counts the cameras. Beat: wary calculation—he needs Noor as much as she needs him.

chapters.title: The Green Zone
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Escorted into the walled enclave of safehouses where deniable witnesses are kept, she meets Voss through glass. He says one word—'Yarrow'—proving he knows her family's flight. Beat: vertigo; her invisibility was never real.

chapters.title: What the Manifest Forgot
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Voss reveals 9C's passenger list was rewritten in flight by a system called LATTICE, the same signature found in Flight 447's final minutes. Beat: fury and hope braided together—the conspiracy has a name.

chapters.title: Handlers
chapters.summary: Deputy coordinator Marsh's POV. Marsh reports to unseen superiors that Voss is ready to be moved—and that Noor's involvement is 'acceptable collateral.' Beat: institutional menace; power treating people as line items.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Leaving the Zone, she notices the same gray sedan across three days. Her apartment has been searched but left neat. Beat: paranoia crystallizing into resolve—she stops hiding and starts preparing.

chapters.title: LATTICE
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Flashback to building the records-erasure system and the moment he learned it was being used on passenger flights, not just enemy archives. Beat: guilt—he didn't pull the trigger, but he built the gun.

chapters.title: The Second Safehouse
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Her contact Renn moves her to a backup house after the first is burned. There she finds prior occupants' notes—investigators who asked the same questions and disappeared. Beat: dread deepening into defiance.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Math
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She maps the border checkpoint's shift changes: a nineteen-minute window at 03:40 when the north lane runs on skeleton crew. Voss insists they move tomorrow; Noor smells manipulation. Beat: tension between urgency and suspicion.

chapters.title: Bait Theory
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Noor lays out the possibility that Voss is chummed water meant to draw out everyone who remembers 447. Voss neither confirms nor denies, offering instead a fragment of proof only someone inside LATTICE could have. Beat: trust stretched to breaking.

chapters.title: Renn's Price
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. The fixer weighs selling Noor out against a debt owed to the dead of another erased flight. He chooses loyalty—but makes a call that will cost him. Beat: moral compromise with a conscience.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. Orders come down: extract Voss tonight via the south gate; Noor is to be 'retired from the file.' Marsh hesitates for the first time in twenty years. Beat: the machinery of power showing a hairline crack.

chapters.title: Nineteen Minutes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The extraction begins early and wrong—Marsh's team hits the second safehouse. Noor and Voss flee through drainage tunnels as the house burns behind them. Beat: adrenaline, betrayal confirmed, clock started.

chapters.title: The Gray Sedan
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Pursued to a rail yard, Noor turns the tables using her investigator's eye for patterns, disabling the tail car and learning its driver is the same man who followed her from day one—an old colleague from the 447 inquiry. Beat: rage with a target.

chapters.title: Confession at Kilometer Nine
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Cornered between teams, Voss admits he was sent as bait—but he also smuggled out the LATTICE master key, choosing Noor over his handlers. Beat: redemption offered, not yet earned.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Climax at the border: 03:21, the checkpoint alert, Marsh arriving personally to stop them. Noor broadcasts the 447 and 9C manifests over the checkpoint's own radio, making every guard a witness. Beat: the climax—truth as a weapon fired in public.

chapters.title: Crossing
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the chaos, guards refuse orders; Marsh retreats rather than shoot witnesses. Voss is shot covering Noor's crossing and dies at kilometer nine, the key in her hand. Beat: victory purchased with loss.

chapters.title: The Record
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. From outside the country, she releases the manifests, the LATTICE key, and the names of the vanished investigators—including row twelve's true cause. News breaks globally; inquiries open. Beat: catharsis—justice outside the law, finally written down.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. Testifying under immunity, Marsh chooses truth over the institution, naming the order-givers. Some walk free; the system itself is exposed. Beat: bitter, necessary accountability—corruption named if not fully punished.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. One year later, Noor testifies openly, her name attached to the reopened 447 docket. At the memorial, she reads row twelve aloud. Beat: resolution—she stopped being invisible, and the dead are remembered.
